questions: Did s-bend progress rise above 0.04, and did its max_error fall below 0.061 m?
Did steering_oscillation stay below 0.16 on all tracks with the 0.05 m forward offset?
Did slalom progress return to about 0.10 (versus 0.035 in iteration 4), and does the single line-loss event remain?
Did any track complete? If not, which track ended off track first, and at what progress?
Is the s-bend failure at the same progress point (about 0.04) with y = 0.05 m? If so, forward lead is not the lever.
feedback_request.what_to_report: Per track (oval, s-bend, slalom): completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors. Also the kp that gave the best rms_error with this layout, and which sensors carry the most signal on the line.

intent: Test whether forward sensor lead fixes the s-bend turn-rate lag. Move all seven 16 mm contiguous sensors from y = 0.03 m to y = 0.05 m, and revert wheel_track and mass to 0.12 m and 0.8 kg, the iteration 2 values that gave the best oval and slalom progress. The sensing layout is otherwise unchanged, so the result isolates forward offset. Expect s-bend progress above 0.04, slalom progress at or above 0.104, and no oval line loss.
learning: Iteration 4 showed that wheel_track 0.10 m and mass 0.6 kg do not change the s-bend result (progress 0.04 both times), so the turn-rate hypothesis is weakened. Iteration 4 also showed that 20 mm pitch with 16 mm sensors removes slalom line loss but cuts slalom progress from 0.104 to 0.035. Sensor pitch should stay contiguous. This iteration tests forward lead (y = 0.05 m) as the next lever for the s-bend, holding all other geometry at the iteration 2 values.
rationale: Race evidence from iterations 2 to 4 points to three conclusions. (1) The contiguous 16 mm layout at x = ±0.048 m removed line loss on the oval and s-bend (0 events each), so sensing footprint is no longer the limit there. (2) The s-bend fails at progress 0.04 with max_error about 0.061 m and zero line loss in every run since iteration 2. Kp 5.0 changed nothing (iteration 3 was identical to iteration 2). In iteration 4, wheel_track 0.10 m and mass 0.6 kg also left s-bend progress at exactly 0.04 with max_error 0.0605 m. Turn rate is therefore not the binding constraint, and the robot is leaving the tape at a fixed point regardless of drivetrain. The likely cause is that the sensors reach the bend too late, so the controller starts responding after the robot is already committed. (3) Iteration 4's 20 mm pitch removed slalom line loss (0 events), but slalom progress fell from 0.104 to 0.035 and the robot went off track earlier, so the wider pitch with 16 mm sensors leaves the centre under-resolved. I revert that pitch and the drivetrain to the iteration 2 values (16 mm contiguous at ±0.048 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg), which had the best progress on the oval and slalom. The one change is a forward sensor offset of y = 0.05 m instead of 0.03 m, giving about 2 cm more lead. Steering oscillation has stayed at 0.07 to 0.14, well below the 0.16 trigger, so there is room for more lead. Expected result: s-bend progress above 0.04 (the first sign of a fix for the turn-rate lag), slalom progress at or above 0.104, and oval line loss still at 0. If s-bend progress is still 0.04 with y = 0.05 m, forward lead is not the fix and the next test is a larger lever (for example y = 0.07 m or a shorter wheel track of 0.08 m).
